HTTP snapshot request and redirect parsing for snapshot slot resolution.

# Purpose
`fd_ssresolve.c` implements a small HTTP-based snapshot resolver. It creates and manages an internal state machine that sends a `GET` request for either `snapshot.tar.bz2` or `incremental-snapshot.tar.bz2`, then reads the HTTP response from a socket and parses it with `picohttpparser`. The file defines the memory layout helpers [`fd_ssresolve_align`](<#fd_ssresolve_align>), [`fd_ssresolve_footprint`](<#fd_ssresolve_footprint>), [`fd_ssresolve_new`](<#fd_ssresolve_new>), and [`fd_ssresolve_join`](<#fd_ssresolve_join>), which set up and validate the shared object used by the resolver.

The main runtime logic is in [`fd_ssresolve_init`](<#fd_ssresolve_init>), [`fd_ssresolve_advance_poll_out`](<#fd_ssresolve_advance_poll_out>), and [`fd_ssresolve_advance_poll_in`](<#fd_ssresolve_advance_poll_in>). The resolver sends the request in nonblocking mode, waits for a response, and handles HTTP redirect status codes by reading the `Location` header. It then uses `fd_ssarchive_parse_filename` to extract snapshot slot values from the redirect target and stores the result in `fd_ssresolve_result_t`. The file also defines [`fd_ssresolve_is_done`](<#fd_ssresolve_is_done>) to report when resolution has finished.
